newsitem.title: USA: Aides with big titles drain Clinton travel budget.
newsitem.headline: Aides with big titles drain Clinton travel budget.

text.p: President Bill Clinton has taken so many aides with him on his frequent travels that his travel budget is rapidly approaching zero, the White House said on Monday.
Spokesman Mike McCurry said part of the problem was people wangling their way onto presidential trips by "taking seriously the inflated titles that they've been given."

With the end of the current fiscal year coming up Sept. 30, Clinton has $40,000 left out of a $814,000 travel budget for presidential support staff. The budget period goes back to last Oct. 1, which was during the heat of Clinton's re-election campaign when he travelled heavily.

To stretch it out he is taking a skeleton crew with him for his three-week vacation on the Massachusetts island of Martha's Vineyard starting next Sunday. He still has one or two other long trips planned for later in September.
Clinton, asked if he was running out of travel money, told reporters: "I hope not. I'm trying to go on holiday."

White House deputy chief of staff John Podesta has been assigned to personally approve each official traveller on Air Force One and other government business. This does not apply to the Secret Service, White House doctors or military personnel.

McCurry said Clinton and his wife Hillary Rodham Clinton have expressed some concern about the number of staff aides going along on their trips and "would like to keep the size of their entourage to a minimum."

McCurry denied a report in U.S. News and World Report that money was so tight, a senior White House official agreed to pay out of his own pocket the air fare for press deputy Joe Lockhart to relieve another press aide, Barry Toiv, during the Martha's Vineyard vacation.
The spokesman said it was a staple of White House life that aides want to go on trips whether needed or not.
"I've yet to be on a presidential trip where you don't feel there are too many people on it," he said.
